items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: I met his wife. Yeah, I see. The Chippy Keelan.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Not, not Frankie. Frank Keelan. The trumpet player?

Uh-huh. So. I met his wife. Yeah, I see. The Chippy Keelan. Uh-huh. All the brothers, there was, there was, there was the bunch back there, the battlefield, eh? Uh, Willi Peen, Keelan, and, uh, Baker, James Baker, all that bunch back there. You see, that was, the basin was back there. Uh-huh. Old basin. And the schooners would come in, old, come in as far as, up here as far as, uh, uh, uh, uh, de Radda. Uh-huh. Before you get to Ramport Street there, they had, uh, the schooners would, that's how far as, uh, uh,…

basin would run. And they had a whole steamboat, the steamboat, what you call a lumber yard the boats used to bring in lumber from different parts of the over the lake, you see, like Mandeville, Madison, Madison Lumber Company, we'd send, they'd have big boatloads of green lumber would come in. And them guys in that battlefield they used to play, shoot dice on a candlelight back at Bertrand and between Portis and Lafayette. Well you were living on Balabar then. I was living on Balabar between Gravy and Padida.…
